# Purpose

This is the **identity-scale** companion to the two ratio-scale ACTG175 documents: a continuous outcome, a
**mean difference** in place of an odds or hazard ratio, and thresholds in **CD4 cells per mm³**.

One forest-search fit selects the subgroup under the max N(ε) criterion, and multiplier resampling (MR), computed
inside the same fit, gives the selection-adjusted bounds the operating-characteristics simulations evaluate: the
**field** one-sided lower bound on $\beta(\hat H)$, the **field-s** one-sided upper bound on $\beta(\hat H^c)$, and
the **Bonferroni pair** joining them. Beside them are the **unadjusted** analysis and the **two-term de-biased
estimate**, whose two-sided IJ interval is a reference only. Quantities that exist only in simulation are not
reported. No full bootstrap, cross-validation, DINA or GRF analysis is run, and **no operating-characteristics
section is run**: nothing here calls the `fs_oc_*` machinery.

**Every setting comes from an applied analysis of these data:**
`forestsearch/quarto/applications/actg175/analysis_actg175_continuous_oc.qmd`, cited line by line below.
**One deliberate departure:** `sg_focus` and `effect_neighborhood` are this workstream's, §1.1.

::: {.callout-important}
## The harm direction: positive is harm, and the treated arm is the combination

The outcome is **`y_decline = cd40 − cd420`**, the CD4 **decline** from baseline to week 20 (applied document
line 66), so it is adverse as it stands: larger means a worse CD4 outcome. `adverse_outcome = TRUE` (line 100)
therefore applies **no** further negation, and **`treat = 1` is arm 1, zidovudine + didanosine** (line 64), the
trial's own coding.

**Exactly one orientation flip is in effect**, and it is in the outcome's construction. So **a positive mean
difference means a worse CD4 outcome under ZDV + ddI — harm from the experimental arm** — and the unit is CD4
cells per mm³, with the null at **0**. The raw `cd4_change = cd420 − cd40` scale is this scale's sign flip. The
`setup` chunk asserts the direction against a direct fit rather than asserting it in a comment.
:::

## 1.1 The one departure, and why it is safe here

The applied document runs **`maxeffCons`** (line 102) and sets no `effect_neighborhood`. **This analysis runs
`sg_focus = "effMaxSG"` with `effect_neighborhood = 0.20`**, the rule GBSG, panitumumab and the binary ACTG175
analysis all use, so that this workstream's four analyses answer the same question.

The applied document uses `maxeffCons` because its **operating-characteristics** sections require it: the
`fs_oc_*` functions implement only that selection and read neither `effect_neighborhood` nor `selection_rule`
(finding F1 of `REPORT_actg175_applied_effmaxsg_stage0_2026-09-16.md`). **This document runs no such section**, so
the constraint does not apply here. Both rules' anchors are recorded in that report's §6, and the `effMaxSG` one is
reproduced below.

## Subgroup descriptions

Subgroup definitions are carried in the payloads in the search's own coding; in this document's tables and prose
they are rendered in plain language. A negated comparison is flipped, so `cd40 <= 507` negated reads "baseline CD4
count > 507 per mm³". A flag takes its own or its complement's label. Every label comes from the
`speff2trial::ACTG175` documentation: `race` is 0 white and 1 non-white; `gender` is 0 female and 1 male; `homo`
is homosexual activity; `drugs` a history of intravenous drug use; `symptom` the symptomatic indicator; `karnof`
the Karnofsky score on a 0–100 scale; `preanti` days of previously received antiretroviral therapy; `cd40` and
`cd80` the baseline CD4 and CD8 T cell counts, in the per-cubic-millimetre units the trial's eligibility range is
quoted in.

```{r label-map}
covariate_labels <- data.frame(
  covariate  = c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80",
                 "hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom"),
  label      = c("age", "prior antiretroviral therapy", "weight", "Karnofsky score",
                 "baseline CD4 count", "baseline CD8 count",
                 "hemophilia", "homosexual activity", "history of intravenous drug use",
                 "non-white", "male", "symptomatic"),
  unit       = c("years", "days", "kg", "", "per mm³", "per mm³", "", "", "", "", "", ""),
  complement = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA,
                 "no hemophilia", "no homosexual activity", "no history of intravenous drug use",
                 "white", "female", "asymptomatic"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(transform(covariate_labels, unit = ifelse(nzchar(unit), unit, "—"),
                       complement = ifelse(is.na(complement), "—", complement)),
             col.names = c("Covariate", "Label", "Unit", "Complement label"), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Covariate label map (the translation table itself), from the speff2trial::ACTG175 documentation.")

.parse_term <- function(term) {
  term <- trimws(term)
  neg  <- startsWith(term, "!")
  body <- sub("^!?\\{(.*)\\}$", "\\1", term)
  m <- regmatches(body, regexec("^([A-Za-z0-9_.]+)\\s*(<=|>=|<|>|==)\\s*(\\S+)$", body))[[1]]
  if (length(m) == 4L) list(var = m[2], op = m[3], value = as.numeric(m[4]), neg = neg)
  else list(var = body, op = NA_character_, value = NA_real_, neg = neg)
}
.flip <- c("<=" = ">", ">=" = "<", "<" = ">=", ">" = "<=")
.sym  <- c("<=" = "≤", ">=" = "≥", "<" = "<", ">" = ">", "==" = "=")
describe_subgroup <- function(def) {
  terms <- strsplit(def, " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  out <- vapply(terms, function(tm) {
    p <- .parse_term(tm); i <- match(p$var, covariate_labels$covariate)
    if (is.na(i)) stop("no label for covariate ", p$var)
    if (is.na(p$op)) {
      if (!p$neg) return(covariate_labels$label[i])
      if (is.na(covariate_labels$complement[i])) stop("no complement label for ", p$var)
      return(covariate_labels$complement[i])
    }
    op <- if (p$neg) .flip[[p$op]] else p$op
    trimws(sprintf("%s %s %s %s", covariate_labels$label[i], .sym[[op]], format(p$value), covariate_labels$unit[i]))
  }, character(1))
  paste(out, collapse = " and ")
}
# the same rule, evaluated. The binary covariates are factors, as the applied document builds
# them (line 67), so a flag term compares on the level.
subgroup_member <- function(def, d) {
  terms <- strsplit(def, " & ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  Reduce(`&`, lapply(terms, function(tm) {
    p <- .parse_term(tm); x <- d[[p$var]]; stopifnot(!is.null(x))
    v <- if (is.na(p$op)) as.character(x) == "1" else {
      x <- as.numeric(as.character(x))
      switch(p$op, "<=" = x <= p$value, ">=" = x >= p$value,
             "<" = x < p$value, ">" = x > p$value, "==" = x == p$value)
    }
    if (p$neg) !v else v
  }))
}
# Gate 7.1: a description carries no coding characters and no column name, and denotes the payload's set (by N)
raw_names <- c("preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80", "cd420", "cd4_change", "y_decline",
               "hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom", "str2", "arms")
check_description <- function(def, N, d) {
  s <- describe_subgroup(def)
  bad <- grepl("[{}!]", s) || any(vapply(raw_names, function(k) grepl(paste0("\\b", k, "\\b"), s), TRUE))
  if (bad) stop("description still carries coding: ", s)
  if (sum(subgroup_member(def, d)) != N) stop("description of ", def, " does not give N = ", N)
  s
}
```

# Data

The preparation is the applied document's, line for line.

```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(forestsearch)
  library(speff2trial)
})
t_doc <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]

cont_vars <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")     # applied document line 58
bin_vars  <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom")   # line 59
confounders <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)                                  # line 60

df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))                # line 62
n_arms13  <- nrow(df)
df$id     <- seq_len(nrow(df))                                         # line 63
df$treat  <- ifelse(df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)                             # line 64: ZDV + ddI = 1
n_dropped <- sum(is.na(df$cd420))
df <- df[!is.na(df$cd420), ]                                           # line 65
df$y_decline <- df$cd40 - df$cd420                                     # line 66: a decline, positive = harm
for (v in bin_vars) df[[v]] <- as.factor(df[[v]])                      # line 67

stopifnot(n_arms13 == 1083, nrow(df) == 1083, n_dropped == 0,
          !anyNA(df[c(confounders, "y_decline", "treat")]),
          sum(df$treat == 1) == sum(df$arms == 1L))                     # treat = 1 IS the combination arm

# The harm direction, asserted rather than commented: the oriented mean difference equals
# mean(y_decline | ZDV+ddI) - mean(y_decline | ddI), so a POSITIVE value means a larger CD4
# decline -- a worse outcome -- under ZDV + ddI. Exactly one flip is in effect: y_decline is
# already adverse and adverse_outcome = TRUE applies no further negation.
md_whole <- coef(lm(y_decline ~ treat, data = df))[[2]]
stopifnot(abs(md_whole - (mean(df$y_decline[df$treat == 1]) - mean(df$y_decline[df$treat == 0]))) < 1e-9,
          abs(md_whole + coef(lm(I(cd420 - cd40) ~ treat, data = df))[[2]]) < 1e-9)   # the raw scale is its sign flip
c(subjects = nrow(df), ZDV_ddI = sum(df$treat == 1), ddI = sum(df$treat == 0),
  dropped_missing_week20_CD4 = n_dropped,
  whole_trial_oriented_MD = round(md_whole, 3),
  mean_decline_ZDV_ddI = round(mean(df$y_decline[df$treat == 1]), 1),
  mean_decline_ddI = round(mean(df$y_decline[df$treat == 0]), 1))
```

## Reference effects

Each bound below is read against the whole-trial effect and against the marginal strata of the covariates that
define the selected subgroup, never against MD 0 alone.

```{r reference-effects}
# Oriented mean difference on y_decline: positive = worse CD4 outcome under ZDV + ddI.
md_est <- function(d, min_per_arm = 0) {
  n <- tapply(d$y_decline, factor(d$treat, levels = 0:1), length)
  n[is.na(n)] <- 0L
  out <- data.frame(n = nrow(d), n_ctrl = n[["0"]], n_trt = n[["1"]],
                    mean_ctrl = NA_real_, mean_trt = NA_real_,
                    md = NA_real_, lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_)
  if (min(n) < max(2, min_per_arm)) return(out)
  out$mean_ctrl <- mean(d$y_decline[d$treat == 0])
  out$mean_trt  <- mean(d$y_decline[d$treat == 1])
  f  <- lm(y_decline ~ treat, data = d)
  b  <- coef(f)[[2]]; se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(f)))[[2]]
  out$md <- b; out$lo <- b - qnorm(0.975) * se; out$hi <- b + qnorm(0.975) * se
  out
}
f1  <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", sprintf("%.1f", x))
fci <- function(e, l, u) ifelse(is.na(e), "—", sprintf("%.1f (%.1f, %.1f)", e, l, u))

ref_sets <- list(
  "whole trial"                    = rep(TRUE, nrow(df)),
  "baseline CD4 > 507 per mm³"     = df$cd40 > 507,
  "baseline CD4 ≤ 507 per mm³"     = df$cd40 <= 507,
  "male"                           = as.character(df$gender) == "1",
  "female"                         = as.character(df$gender) == "0")
reference_md <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ref_sets), function(k)
  cbind(set = k, md_est(df[ref_sets[[k]], ]))))
rownames(reference_md) <- NULL
knitr::kable(data.frame(set = reference_md$set, N = reference_md$n,
                        `ZDV+ddI / ddI` = sprintf("%d / %d", reference_md$n_trt, reference_md$n_ctrl),
                        `mean CD4 decline (ZDV+ddI / ddI)` = sprintf("%s / %s", f1(reference_md$mean_trt), f1(reference_md$mean_ctrl)),
                        `oriented MD (95% CI)` = fci(reference_md$md, reference_md$lo, reference_md$hi),
                        check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Mean difference in CD4 decline to week 20, CD4 cells per mm³: positive means a worse CD4 outcome under ZDV + ddI. A negative value is benefit from the combination.")
```

# The fit

One call. Identification, the unadjusted estimates and every MR quantity come out of it together. Every argument is
the applied document's, at its line, except `sg_focus` and `effect_neighborhood` (§1.1).

```{r fit}
mr_draws <- 5000L
t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
fit <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = df, confounders.name = confounders,
  outcome.name = "y_decline", treat.name = "treat", id.name = "id",      # lines 95-97
  outcome_type = "continuous", effect_measure = "MD",                    # lines 98-99
  adverse_outcome = TRUE,                                                # line 100
  seedit = 8316951,                                                      # line 101 (params$seed)
  sg_focus = "effMaxSG", effect_neighborhood = 0.20,                     # THIS WORKSTREAM'S DEPARTURE (§1.1)
  selection_rule = "neighborhood",                                       # line 103
  consistency_method = "resample",                                       # line 104
  effect.threshold = 10, consistency.threshold = 5,                      # lines 105-106
  pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,                                         # line 107
  use_twostage = TRUE,                                                   # line 108
  conf.cont_jcuts = list(age = 10, preanti = 10, wtkg = 10,              # lines 109-110
                         karnof = 10, cd40 = 10, cd80 = 10),
  cut_type = "default", maxk = 2L, n.min = 60L,                          # lines 111-113
  d0.min = 10L, d1.min = 10L, fs.splits = 500L,                          # lines 114-116
  use_lasso = FALSE, use_grf = FALSE, use_dina = FALSE, is.RCT = TRUE,   # lines 117-120
  mr_inference = TRUE,                                                   # line 128
  mr_inference_args = list(ci_method = "field", draws = mr_draws,        # lines 129-134
                           include_complement = TRUE, field_complement = TRUE,
                           field_scale_complement = "selected",
                           return_reselection = TRUE,
                           keep_declaration_field = TRUE, keep_field_matrix = FALSE,
                           declaration_c0 = c(-5, -10, -15)))
fit_sec <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
if (fit_sec > 900) stop(sprintf("the fit took %.0f s, over the 15-minute cap", fit_sec))
g <- fit$mr_inference
cat(sprintf("forestsearch %s; fit including MR: %.1f s (multiplier stage %.1f s; field blocks %.1f + %.1f s)\n",
            packageVersion("forestsearch"), fit_sec, g$timing_seconds,
            g$field$timing_seconds, g$field$complement$timing_seconds))
```

## The settings the package received, and that MR ran

Read back from the fit's own record of its arguments. The printed configuration, which names the measure, the
scale and the resolved thresholds, is in the fit's console output above.

```{r settings-received}
keys <- c("outcome_type", "effect_measure", "adverse_outcome", "effect.threshold", "consistency.threshold",
          "pconsistency.threshold", "consistency_method", "sg_focus", "selection_rule", "effect_neighborhood",
          "max_subgroups_search", "n.min", "d0.min", "d1.min", "maxk", "fs.splits")
received <- fit$args_call_all[keys]
knitr::kable(data.frame(argument = keys,
                        received = vapply(received, function(x) paste(format(x), collapse = ", "), "")),
             row.names = FALSE, caption = "fit$args_call_all, as recorded by forestsearch().")
stopifnot(identical(received$outcome_type, "continuous"), identical(received$effect_measure, "MD"),
          isTRUE(received$adverse_outcome),
          received$effect.threshold == 10, received$consistency.threshold == 5,
          received$pconsistency.threshold == 0.9,
          identical(received$consistency_method, "resample"),
          received$sg_focus %in% c("effMaxSG", "hrMaxSG"),      # recorded canonically
          identical(received$selection_rule, "neighborhood"), received$effect_neighborhood == 0.20,
          is.infinite(received$max_subgroups_search),           # the document sets none
          received$n.min == 60, received$d0.min == 10, received$d1.min == 10,
          received$maxk == 2, received$fs.splits == 500)

# Gate 5.1: MR ran, checked on the returned object. On MD the working scale is the outcome's own,
# so log_scale is FALSE and the near-null confirmation point is 0.
stopifnot(!is.null(g), is.list(g$field), is.list(g$field$complement), is.list(g$field$joint_s),
          !is.na(fit$mr_harm_confirmed), is.finite(g$naive$est), is.finite(g$debiased$est),
          is.finite(g$field$lower_1s), is.finite(g$field$complement$upper_1s_s),
          identical(g$measure, "MD"), isFALSE(g$log_scale), g$n_family > 0)
cat(sprintf("MR ran: measure %s, log scale %s, family %d, harm confirmed %s (rule %s, t_confirm %s).\n",
            g$measure, g$log_scale, g$n_family, fit$mr_harm_confirmed,
            g$settings$confirm_rule, format(g$settings$t_confirm)))
```

## The selection, the anchor, and the candidate funnel

The applied document's own record, `REPORT_actg175_applied_effmaxsg_stage0_2026-09-16.md` §6, computed both rules'
anchors on these data and settings with MR off. **This fit must reproduce its `effMaxSG` row.**

```{r selection}
label_fs <- paste(fit$sg.harm, collapse = " & ")
est <- fit$df.est
in_H <- est$treat.recommend[match(df$id, est$id)] == 0
stopifnot(!anyNA(in_H), identical(in_H, subgroup_member(label_fs, df)))
n_H <- sum(in_H); n_Hc <- sum(!in_H)
md_H <- md_est(df[in_H, ])$md
cand <- as.data.frame(fit$grp.consistency$out_sg$result)
pcons_H <- cand$Pcons[1]

anchor <- data.frame(
  check = c("subgroup", "n", "oriented MD", "Pcons"),
  recorded = c(describe_subgroup("!{cd40 <= 507} & {gender}"), "79", "71.10", "0.91"),
  this_fit = c(describe_subgroup(label_fs), n_H, sprintf("%.2f", md_H), sprintf("%.2f", pcons_H)))
knitr::kable(anchor, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Gate 3.1: the effMaxSG anchor of REPORT_actg175_applied_effmaxsg_stage0_2026-09-16.md §6.")
if (!identical(label_fs, "!{cd40 <= 507} & {gender}") || n_H != 79L ||
    abs(md_H - 71.10) > 0.005 || abs(pcons_H - 0.91) > 0.005)
  stop("the fit does not reproduce the recorded effMaxSG anchor")

fcn <- fit$find.grps$filter_counts
funnel <- data.frame(
  stage = c("candidates enumerated", "passing the variance and prevalence checks", "passing redundancy",
            "passing the per-arm minimum (10 / 10)", "clearing the screen (MD ≥ 10, oriented)",
            "evaluated for consistency", "passing consistency (c2 = 5, p* = 0.90)",
            "on the Pareto frontier", "MR candidate family"),
  n = c(fcn$n_evaluated, fcn$n_passed_prevalence, fcn$n_passed_redundancy, fcn$n_passed_sample_size,
        fcn$n_passed_hr, fit$grp.consistency$n_candidates_evaluated, fit$grp.consistency$n_passed,
        nrow(fit$grp.consistency$out_sg$pareto_frontier), g$n_family))
knitr::kable(funnel, col.names = c("", "count"), row.names = FALSE, caption = "The candidate funnel.")

# the consistency-passing candidates. On this path the package's `hr` column is the effect on the
# working (identity) scale, with no transform to undo, and `E` repeats `N`: a continuous outcome
# has no events.
mcols <- grep("^M\\.", names(cand), value = TRUE)
cand_def <- apply(cand[, mcols, drop = FALSE], 1, function(z) paste(z[nzchar(z) & !is.na(z)], collapse = " & "))
cand_tab <- data.frame(
  subgroup = vapply(seq_along(cand_def), function(i) check_description(cand_def[i], cand$N[i], df), ""),
  N = cand$N, `oriented MD` = sprintf("%.1f", cand$hr), Pcons = sprintf("%.2f", cand$Pcons),
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(cand_tab, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf("All %d candidates passing consistency, ordered as the package returns them; the first row is the max N(ε) selection. Mean differences in CD4 cells per mm³, oriented.", nrow(cand)))
stopifnot(abs(cand$hr[1] - md_H) < 1e-8, cand$N[1] == n_H, identical(unname(cand_def[1]), label_fs))
```

# The data set

```{r cascade}
cascade <- data.frame(
  population = c("Trial, four arms", "Arms 1 and 3", "Analysis set", "Selected / complement"),
  N = c(format(nrow(speff2trial::ACTG175)), format(n_arms13), format(nrow(df)),
        sprintf("%d / %d", n_H, n_Hc)),
  what_it_is = c(
    "every subject in the package's data set; the other two arms are not analysed",
    "arm 1 (ZDV + ddI) and arm 3 (ddI), the applied document's subset",
    sprintf("arms 1 and 3 less %d with no week-20 CD4 count, the only exclusion; %d on ZDV + ddI, %d on ddI",
            n_dropped, sum(df$treat == 1), sum(df$treat == 0)),
    "the max N(ε) split"))
knitr::kable(cascade, col.names = c("Population", "N", "What it is"), align = "lrl", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "The counts.")
```

# Selection-adjusted bounds

```{r extract}
cc <- g$complement
fb <- g$field
fc <- fb$complement
js <- fb$joint_s

bounds <- list(
  field_lower_H     = fb$lower_1s,
  field_s_upper_Hc  = fc$upper_1s_s,
  bonf_lower_H      = js$bonf_lower_H,
  bonf_upper_Hc     = js$bonf_upper_Hc,
  bonf_joint_prob   = js$bonf_joint_prob,
  calib_gamma       = js$gamma,
  calib_joint_prob  = js$joint_prob,
  calib_lower_H     = js$lower_H,
  calib_upper_Hc    = js$upper_Hc,
  joint_corr        = js$corr,
  n_joint_draws     = js$n_joint_draws,
  # the applied document does not pass field_decompose (package default FALSE), so the
  # complement's decomposition fields, and with them the scale ratio rho-c, are not computed
  rho_c             = if (is.null(fc$decomp_fields)) NA_real_ else fc$decomp_fields$scale_ratio_c,
  n_out_H           = fb$n_out_used,
  n_in_H            = fb$n_in_used_mean,
  n_out_Hc          = fc$n_out_used,
  field_sec_H       = fb$timing_seconds,
  field_sec_Hc      = fc$timing_seconds,
  alpha             = js$alpha,
  # est2 = two-term - lambda_mean on the WORKING scale, here the identity scale, so lambda_mean
  # is itself a number of CD4 cells and the correction is a subtraction, not a ratio
  field_est2_H            = fb$est2,
  field_lambda_mean_H     = fb$lambda_mean,
  field_s_est2_Hc         = fc$est2_s,
  field_s_lambda_mean_Hc  = fc$lambda_mean_s,
  field_est2_Hc           = fc$est2,
  field_lambda_mean_Hc    = fc$lambda_mean)
stopifnot(is.finite(bounds$field_est2_H), is.finite(bounds$field_lambda_mean_H),
          is.finite(bounds$field_s_est2_Hc), is.finite(bounds$field_s_lambda_mean_Hc),
          abs(bounds$field_est2_H - (g$debiased$est - bounds$field_lambda_mean_H)) < 1e-9,
          abs(bounds$field_s_est2_Hc - (cc$debiased$est - bounds$field_s_lambda_mean_Hc)) < 1e-9)

whole <- reference_md[1, ]
ci <- function(l, u) sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", l, u)
summary_table <- data.frame(
  row = c("**Reference effects**", "Whole trial",
          "**Identified subgroup**", "Unadjusted", "Two-term", "Field, lower bound",
          "**Complement**", "Unadjusted", "Two-term", "Field-s, upper bound"),
  N = c("", whole$n, "", n_H, n_H, n_H, "", n_Hc, n_Hc, n_Hc),
  MD = c("", f1(whole$md), "",
         f1(g$naive$est), f1(g$debiased$est), f1(bounds$field_est2_H), "",
         f1(cc$naive$est), f1(cc$debiased$est), f1(bounds$field_s_est2_Hc)),
  CI = c("", ci(whole$lo, whole$hi), "",
         ci(g$naive$lower, g$naive$upper), paste(ci(g$debiased$lower, g$debiased$upper), "†"),
         paste(f1(bounds$field_lower_H), "‡"), "",
         ci(cc$naive$lower, cc$naive$upper), paste(ci(cc$debiased$lower, cc$debiased$upper), "†"),
         paste(f1(bounds$field_s_upper_Hc), "‡")),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(summary_table, col.names = c("", "N", "MD", "95% CI"), align = "lrrl", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf("Mean difference in CD4 decline to week 20, **CD4 cells per mm³**: positive means a worse CD4 outcome under ZDV + ddI, negative means benefit from it. Whole trial: %d on ZDV + ddI, %d on ddI. Identified subgroup: %s.",
                               whole$n_trt, whole$n_ctrl, check_description(label_fs, n_H, df)))
```

† Two-sided infinitesimal-jackknife interval, reference only.

‡ One-sided 95%, inverted around the two-term estimate. Bonferroni pair, joint 95%:
`r f1(bounds$bonf_lower_H)` and `r f1(bounds$bonf_upper_Hc)`.

**There is no events column**, which a continuous outcome has no use for; the arms' mean CD4 decline stands in its
place in the reference table. Mean differences are given to **one decimal**: the whole-trial standard error is
about 8 cells, so more digits would be spurious. **The raw `cd4_change` scale is the sign flip of every number
here.**

```{r est2-reading, echo = FALSE}
ord_H <- bounds$field_lower_H <= bounds$field_est2_H && bounds$field_est2_H <= g$debiased$est
first_H <- g$naive$est - g$debiased$est
first_Hc <- cc$naive$est - cc$debiased$est
```

**The field rows.** Their MD is the field's second-order estimate, `est2`: the two-term estimate less the mean of
the simulated root, $\bar\Lambda$. **Both are on the identity scale here**, so $\bar\Lambda$ is itself a number of
CD4 cells and the correction is a subtraction rather than a ratio. The one-sided bound in the same row is **not**
centred on `est2`: it is inverted around the two-term estimate.

- **The identified subgroup.** $\bar\Lambda$ = `r sprintf("%.2f", bounds$field_lambda_mean_H)` CD4 cells, against a
  first correction (unadjusted to two-term) of `r sprintf("%.2f", first_H)`. `est2` is
  `r f1(bounds$field_est2_H)`, against the two-term `r f1(g$debiased$est)`. The ordering bound ≤ `est2` ≤ two-term
  `r if (ord_H) "holds" else "**does not hold**"`
  (`r f1(bounds$field_lower_H)`, `r f1(bounds$field_est2_H)`, `r f1(g$debiased$est)`)`r if (bounds$field_lambda_mean_H <= 0) ": the mean of the simulated root is not positive, so est2 sits at or above the two-term estimate" else ""`.
- **The complement (field-s).** $\bar\Lambda$ = `r sprintf("%.2f", bounds$field_s_lambda_mean_Hc)`, against a first
  correction of `r sprintf("%.2f", first_Hc)`. `est2` is `r f1(bounds$field_s_est2_Hc)`, against the two-term
  `r f1(cc$debiased$est)`.

```{r diagnostics}
diag_tab <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("candidate family (MR)", "selection bias, MD scale (harm side)",
               "selection bias, MD scale (complement)",
               "field outer / mean inner draws used (harm)", "field outer draws used (complement)",
               "Bonferroni pair: simulated joint coverage",
               "calibrated split: gamma, simulated joint coverage",
               "calibrated split: lower (H-hat), upper (complement)",
               "correlation of the aligned roots",
               "scale ratio rho-c (selected complement / re-selections)",
               "wall time (s): fit + MR; MR multiplier stage; harm field; complement field"),
  value = c(format(g$n_family), sprintf("%.2f", g$selection_bias), sprintf("%.2f", cc$selection_bias),
            sprintf("%d / %.0f", bounds$n_out_H, bounds$n_in_H), format(bounds$n_out_Hc),
            sprintf("%.4f", bounds$bonf_joint_prob),
            sprintf("%.3f, %.4f", bounds$calib_gamma, bounds$calib_joint_prob),
            sprintf("%.1f, %.1f", bounds$calib_lower_H, bounds$calib_upper_Hc),
            sprintf("%.3f", bounds$joint_corr),
            if (is.na(bounds$rho_c)) "not computed: the applied document does not pass field_decompose" else sprintf("%.3f", bounds$rho_c),
            sprintf("%.1f; %.1f; %.1f; %.1f", fit_sec, g$timing_seconds,
                    bounds$field_sec_H, bounds$field_sec_Hc)))
knitr::kable(diag_tab, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Supporting quantities. The selection bias is in CD4 cells per mm³, not on a log scale, so it is not comparable with the ratio-scale analyses' figures.")
```

## Each bound against the trial's effect sizes

The ladder spans both directions, because on these data the estimates sit on the benefit side: −60, −40, −20, −10
(benefit from the combination), 0 (no difference), 5 and 10 (the analysis's own c2 and c1), 20 and 40 (harm).

```{r location}
thr <- c(-60, -40, -20, -10, 0, 5, 10, 20, 40)
loc <- data.frame(
  bound = c("field lower, H-hat", "Bonferroni lower, H-hat",
            "field-s upper, complement", "Bonferroni upper, complement"),
  value = c(bounds$field_lower_H, bounds$bonf_lower_H, bounds$field_s_upper_Hc, bounds$bonf_upper_Hc),
  side  = c("lower", "lower", "upper", "upper"))
loc$reads <- ifelse(loc$side == "lower",
  sprintf("effect at least %.1f: benefit larger than %.1f excluded", loc$value, abs(loc$value)),
  sprintf("effect at most %.1f: benefit of at least %.1f established", loc$value, abs(loc$value)))
loc$thresholds_cleared <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(loc)), function(i) {
  hit <- if (loc$side[i] == "lower") thr[loc$value[i] >= thr] else thr[loc$value[i] <= thr]
  if (length(hit)) paste(sprintf("%.0f", hit), collapse = ", ") else "none"
}, character(1))
loc$whole_trial <- sprintf("%.1f", reference_md$md[1])
knitr::kable(loc[, c("bound", "value", "reads", "thresholds_cleared", "whole_trial")],
             digits = 1, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Oriented MD, CD4 cells per mm³, where negative is benefit from ZDV + ddI. A lower bound clears a rung at or below it; an upper bound clears one at or above it. The 'reads' column is written for bounds on the benefit side, which is where these fall.")
```

# Declaration calibration {#sec-declcal}

**Pre-specification.** Stated before any number below was read.

- **The claim.** Harm is claimed at c1 = 10 (the screen) and c2 = 5 (the per-split consistency threshold) on the mean
  difference in CD4 decline, in cells/mm³, harm = MD > 0, exactly as the rest of this document uses them: unchanged.
- **The protected level c0.** The clinically meaningful uniform benefit against which the false-declaration rate is
  controlled. This document states no clinical margin as such, so c0 is **derived** from its own relevance floor,
  the screen's c1 = 10 cells/mm³, mirrored into the benefit direction: c0 ∈ {−5, −10, −15}, **primary −10**, a
  uniform 10-cell smaller CD4 decline under the combination. These are pre-specified constants, never the observed
  whole-trial effect, and all satisfy c0 ≤ c2. This is a derivation, not a stated clinical margin; Larry may replace
  it.
- **α = 0.10**, family-wise, over the pre-reduction candidate family.

**What is computed.** The screen that chose $\hat H$ admits a candidate $g$ when
$T(g) = (\hat\beta(g) - c_2)/\sigma_D(g) \ge$ `r sprintf("%.3f", fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.10)$z_pstar)`, the cutoff the package applies at p\* = 0.90; that is the
closed-form consistency rule, relabelled. Under the shared-multiplier law of the fit's own MR draws, the maximum of
$T$ over the candidate family, with every candidate shifted to sit at c0, has a 0.90 quantile $\hat\kappa_{0.10}$(c0).
The calibrated rule admits $g$ when $T(g) \ge \hat\kappa_{0.10}$(c0), which holds the family-wise probability of
declaring any harm subgroup at 0.10 whenever every candidate's true effect is c0 or better. On this path c1 = 10 exceeds c2 = 5, so admission carries a relevance floor that the
standardized statistic alone does not express: a candidate is admitted when
$\hat\beta(g) \ge \max\{c_1,\; c_2 + \hat\kappa_{0.10}(c_0)\,\sigma_D(g)\}$, which is the form
the calibrated rule takes here and is applied within the calibration itself. A floor can only
remove candidates, so the family-wise guarantee is preserved. The applied set is narrower
still: it intersects that set with the candidates this document's own screen evaluated,
excluding those the per-arm event minima and the near-duplicate reduction removed from the
enumerated family. The table reports the count both before and after that intersection. The field is read from
the 5,000 draws the fit above already made (`keep_declaration_field = TRUE`, with the grid passed as
`declaration_c0`); nothing is redrawn, and the fit's other outputs are unchanged by it. The capture fired, so the
field comes from the fit itself. The calibrated rule is applied on $T(g)$ directly: `forestsearch()` is **not**
re-run: the calibrated rule is applied to $T(g)$ directly, and the settable pair is guidance on what p\* to set.

```{r declcal}
c0_grid <- c(-5, -10, -15); c0_primary <- -10
c1_nat <- 10; c2_nat <- 5; fmt_c0 <- function(x) sprintf("%g", x)   # the claim, CD4 cells/mm³
stopifnot(!is.null(g$declaration_field), identical(g$declaration_field$meta$c0, c0_grid))   # the capture fired
cal    <- fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.10, c0 = c0_grid)
cal_c2 <- fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.10)                  # c0 = NULL: the c2 boundary
cal_05 <- fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.05, c0 = c0_grid)    # stored in the payload, not reported
stopifnot(identical(cal$c0$source, "capture"), cal$n_family_prereduction == g$n_family,
          isTRUE(cal$reduction$replay_check), !is.null(cal$screened),
          length(cal$screened) == fit$grp.consistency$n_candidates_evaluated)
z_scr <- cal$z_pstar   # the p* = 0.90 screen's cutoff as the package applies it (its print's "T >= ...")
stopifnot(length(z_scr) == 1L, is.finite(z_scr), identical(z_scr, cal_c2$z_pstar))
cal
```

```{r declcal-table}
# The family's identifiers are the search's factor codes: q<i>.1 is the i-th evaluated factor, q<i>.0 its negation.
fam_def <- function(id) vapply(strsplit(id, " & ", fixed = TRUE), function(p) {
  i <- as.integer(sub("^q(\\d+)\\.[01]$", "\\1", p))
  paste0(ifelse(endsWith(p, ".0"), "!", ""), "{", fit$confounders.evaluated[i], "}", collapse = " & ")
}, "")
fld  <- g$declaration_field
id_H <- fld$family_id[fld$meta$selected_index]
stopifnot(identical(fam_def(id_H), label_fs))
T_by_candidate <- data.frame(id = names(cal$T_hat), definition = fam_def(names(cal$T_hat)),
                             N = unname(fld$meta$sizes[names(cal$T_hat)]),
                             beta_hat = unname(cal$beta_hat), sigma_D = unname(cal$sigma_D),
                             T = unname(cal$T_hat), screened = names(cal$T_hat) %in% cal$screened)
i_max <- which.max(T_by_candidate$T)
max_T <- as.list(T_by_candidate[i_max, c("id", "definition", "N", "T", "screened")])
T_H   <- cal$T_hat[[id_H]]

# The applied admitted set: the calibrated set over the pre-reduction family, intersected with the
# candidates this document's own screen evaluated. Intersecting can only remove declarations.
adm     <- c(cal$c0$admitted_calibrated, list(c2 = cal_c2$admitted_calibrated))
applied <- lapply(adm, intersect, cal$screened)
tb      <- cal$c0$table
kappa   <- c(tb$kappa_hat, cal_c2$kappa_hat)
# The settable-pair columns, all of them, under the package's names and in its order, for the c0 rows. The c2 row
# comes from the c0 = NULL call, which returns none of them, so its cells are left blank.
st_nm <- c("pstar_settable", "pstar_achievable", "pcons_eff_settable", "z_eff_settable", "z_gap",
           "digits_fine", "pstar_fine", "z_gap_fine")
stopifnot(identical(names(tb)[names(tb) %in% st_nm], st_nm))
st     <- tb[st_nm]
st_fmt <- data.frame(
  pstar_settable     = formatC(st$pstar_settable, format = "f", digits = cal$digits),
  pstar_achievable   = as.character(st$pstar_achievable),
  pcons_eff_settable = formatC(st$pcons_eff_settable, format = "f", digits = cal$digits + 1L),
  z_eff_settable     = sprintf("%.3f", st$z_eff_settable),
  z_gap              = sprintf("%.3f", st$z_gap),
  digits_fine        = sprintf("%d", st$digits_fine),
  pstar_fine         = vapply(seq_len(nrow(st)), function(i) if (is.na(st$digits_fine[i])) "NA" else
                                formatC(st$pstar_fine[i], format = "f", digits = st$digits_fine[i]), ""),
  z_gap_fine         = sprintf("%.4f", st$z_gap_fine))
st_fmt <- rbind(st_fmt, as.data.frame(as.list(setNames(rep("", length(st_nm)), st_nm))))
stopifnot(identical(names(st_fmt), st_nm))
declcal_table <- data.frame(
  c0       = c(paste0(fmt_c0(tb$c0), ifelse(tb$c0 == c0_primary, " (primary)", "")),
               paste0(fmt_c0(c2_nat), ", the c2 boundary (c0 = c2)")),
  kappa    = sprintf("%.3f", kappa),
  st_fmt,
  fw       = sprintf("%.3f", c(tb$fw_size, cal_c2$fw_size)),
  admitted = sprintf("%d (%d)", lengths(applied), lengths(adm)),
  H_cal    = vapply(applied, function(a) if (length(a)) paste(describe_subgroup(fam_def(a)), collapse = "; ")
                    else "none", ""))
knitr::kable(declcal_table, row.names = FALSE, align = paste0("lr", strrep("r", length(st_nm)), "rrl"),
             col.names = c("c0 (MD, cells/mm³)", "κ̂₀.₁₀", paste0("`", st_nm, "`"), "FŴ₀.₁₀ of the p\\* = 0.90 screen at c0",
                           "candidates the calibrated rule admits", "calibrated Ĥ"),
             caption = sprintf("Declaration calibration at α = 0.10. Admitted, k (m): k in the applied set, the calibrated admitted set intersected with the %d candidates this document's screen evaluated; m in the calibrated admitted set over the pre-reduction family of %d.",
                               length(cal$screened), cal$n_family_prereduction))
```

*The settable-pair columns, in the package's words (`?fs_declaration_calibration`), at the fit's
`pconsistency.digits` = `r cal$digits`: `pstar_settable`, the smallest p\* on the 10^−digits grid whose effective
threshold is at or above κ̂(c0); that threshold as `pcons_eff_settable` (Pcons scale) and `z_eff_settable` (z scale);
`z_gap` = `z_eff_settable` − κ̂(c0) (positive = conservative); and `digits_fine` / `pstar_fine` / `z_gap_fine`, the
smallest digits (searched over 1 to 12) at which the gap falls below 0.01, with its p\*. When no p\* ≤ 1 reaches
κ̂(c0) at the fit's digits, `pstar_achievable` is FALSE and the settable columns are NA. This is guidance on what to
set, not an identity: the settable screen is κ̂(c0) rounded up to what the grid can express, so it admits a subset of
what κ̂(c0) admits. The package reports the settable pair for the c₀ rows only.*

*FŴ at c0 is the family-wise probability that the p\* = 0.90 screen declares a harm subgroup if every candidate's
true effect were a uniform benefit of c0 — a property of this trial's candidate family and covariate design, not
an estimate of the trial's realized error rate.*

**The observed statistic.** The maximum of $T$ ranges over the pre-reduction family of
`r format(cal$n_family_prereduction, big.mark = ",")` candidates: every enumerated candidate of at most two factors
meeting the size minimum, before the near-duplicate reduction.

```{r declcal-observed}
obs_tab <- data.frame(c0 = declcal_table$c0, kappa = declcal_table$kappa,
                      gap_max = sprintf("%.3f", kappa - max_T$T), gap_H = sprintf("%.3f", kappa - T_H))
knitr::kable(obs_tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrr",
             col.names = c("c0 (MD, cells/mm³)", "κ̂₀.₁₀", "κ̂ − max T", "κ̂ − T(Ĥ)"),
             caption = sprintf("Maximum over the family: T = %.3f, %s (N %d)%s. The declared subgroup, %s (N %d): T = %.3f. The p* = 0.90 screen's cutoff is %.3f.",
                               max_T$T, check_description(max_T$definition, max_T$N, df), max_T$N,
                               if (max_T$screened) ", among the candidates the screen evaluated" else ", a candidate the screen did not evaluate",
                               describe_subgroup(label_fs), n_H, T_H, z_scr))
```

**The calibrated Ĥ.**

```{r declcal-decision}
# The readings below are written for an empty applied set at every c0; the document stops otherwise.
if (any(lengths(applied) > 0)) stop("the calibrated rule admits a candidate: the calibrated-H section must be rewritten")
stopifnot(max_T$T < min(kappa), identical(max_T$id, names(which.max(cal$T_hat[cal$screened]))))
i_p <- which(tb$c0 == c0_primary)
```

The applied admitted set is empty at every c0 on the grid, and at the c2 boundary. **No subgroup is declared harmful
at {c1, c2} = {`r fmt_c0(c1_nat)`, `r fmt_c0(c2_nat)`} with 10% family-wise protection against a uniform benefit of
MD −10 cells/mm³ or better.** At no c0 on the grid would the observed maximum clear: its closest approach is
`r sprintf("%.3f", min(tb$kappa_hat) - max_T$T)` below $\hat\kappa_{0.10}$ at c0 = `r fmt_c0(tb$c0[which.min(tb$kappa_hat)])`.
The pre-reduction maximum sits on a candidate the screen evaluated, so the intersection removes nothing here. With
no calibrated Ĥ, there are no bounds to set beside the document's.

## Interpretation {#sec-declcal-interpretation}

```{r declcal-interp, echo = FALSE}
fw_p <- tb$fw_size[i_p]; kap_p <- tb$kappa_hat[i_p]
```

- **What FŴ says about the p\* = 0.90 screen.** If every one of these `r format(cal$n_family_prereduction, big.mark = ",")`
  candidates carried a uniform benefit of MD −10 cells/mm³, the screen as run would declare some harm subgroup in
  `r round(100 * fw_p)`% of perturbation draws; with every candidate at the c2 boundary, in
  `r round(100 * cal_c2$fw_size)`%. That is the size of this family and this covariate design, not the trial's
  realized error rate.
- **What the screen's cutoff would have to be.** Holding the family-wise rate at 0.10 against MD −10 cells/mm³
  needs $T(g) \ge$ `r sprintf("%.2f", kap_p)`, against the screen's `r sprintf("%.3f", z_scr)`: a settable p\* of
  `r if (isTRUE(tb$pstar_achievable[i_p])) sprintf("%s (z_gap %.3f)", formatC(tb$pstar_settable[i_p], format = "f", digits = cal$digits), tb$z_gap[i_p]) else sprintf("none at pconsistency.digits = %d (pstar_achievable FALSE, z_gap NA)", cal$digits)` in place of 0.90.
- **Where the observed maximum sits.** It is `r sprintf("%.2f", max_T$T)`, below $\hat\kappa_{0.10}$ at every c0 on the
  grid (`r sprintf("%.2f", min(tb$kappa_hat))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(tb$kappa_hat))`) and at the c2 boundary
  (`r sprintf("%.2f", cal_c2$kappa_hat)`). `r if (identical(max_T$id, id_H)) "It is attained by the declared subgroup itself." else paste0("It is attained by ", describe_subgroup(max_T$definition), ", not by the declared subgroup.")`
- **The declared subgroup.** Its own $T$ is `r sprintf("%.2f", T_H)`: it clears the screen's `r sprintf("%.3f", z_scr)`, which is why it
  was declared, and falls `r sprintf("%.2f", kap_p - T_H)` short of the calibrated cutoff at the primary c0.
- **The calibrated decision at the primary c0.** No subgroup is declared harmful: the p\* = 0.90 screen's declaration of Ĥ does not carry 10% family-wise
  protection against MD −10 cells/mm³.
- **What is unchanged.** The selection, and every bound and estimate reported above, are those of the fit as run;
  the calibration reads that fit and alters none of them.

# The Pareto frontier

Drawn by `forestsearch::plot_pareto_frontier()` as it stands, from this document's fit.

```{r frontier-figure, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4.2}
fr <- as.data.frame(fit$grp.consistency$out_sg$pareto_frontier)
p_frontier <- forestsearch::plot_pareto_frontier(
  fit,
  show_band = TRUE,               # fires: fit$sg_focus is the canonical "hrMaxSG"
  effect_neighborhood = 0.20,
  label_members = TRUE,
  point_size = 3,
  # the default trim clips the leftmost and rightmost member labels at the frame; widening
  # through the function's own xlim argument clears both
  xlim = c(52, 98))
stopifnot(inherits(p_frontier, "ggplot"))

# the axis carries the raw mean difference: no transform to undo on an identity measure
pd  <- p_frontier$data
sel <- pd[which(pd$is_selected), ]
stopifnot(nrow(sel) == 1L, sel$N == n_H, abs(sel$hr - md_H) < 1e-8, sum(pd$is_selected) == 1L,
          isTRUE(all.equal(sort(pd$hr), sort(fr$hr))))   # plotted values equal the frontier's own

ggplot2::ggsave("fig_actg175_continuous_pareto_frontier.png", p_frontier,
                width = 6.5, height = 4.2, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
cat(sprintf("Frontier: %d members, effect axis %.1f to %.1f (oriented MD); selected %s (N %d, MD %.1f).\n",
            nrow(pd), min(pd$hr), max(pd$hr), describe_subgroup(label_fs), sel$N, sel$hr))
p_frontier
```

The shaded band is the ε = 0.20 neighbourhood of the maximum effect, within which max N(ε) takes the largest
subgroup. Member labels carry the search's raw column names, because the package has no covariate lookup — the
same divergence the GBSG and panitumumab figures have from their documents' tables. The axis limits are set
through the function's own `xlim` argument, because its default trim clips the outermost labels; nothing else is
changed, and the package is not modified.

# Interpretation {#sec-interpretation}

```{r interp-values, echo = FALSE}
ref <- setNames(reference_md$md, reference_md$set)
cleared <- setNames(loc$thresholds_cleared, loc$bound)
# the readings below are written for these locations; the document stops if a bound lands elsewhere
stopifnot(ref[["whole trial"]] < 0,                    # the combination is better overall
          g$naive$est > 0, g$debiased$est > 0,         # the selected subgroup looks harmed, unadjusted
          bounds$field_lower_H < 0,                    # its bound does not reach the null
          bounds$field_s_upper_Hc < 0,                 # the complement's benefit is established
          bounds$bonf_upper_Hc < 0, bounds$bonf_lower_H < 0)
```

Every statement below is read from the bound's location on the oriented mean-difference scale, in CD4 cells per
mm³, where **positive means a worse CD4 outcome under ZDV + ddI and negative means benefit from it**. None is a
test at 0. The whole trial's effect is `r f1(ref[["whole trial"]])`: across these two arms the combination spares
about `r sprintf("%.0f", abs(ref[["whole trial"]]))` CD4 cells of decline.

**The selected subgroup.**

- **What was selected.** Max N(ε) returned `r describe_subgroup(label_fs)`: `r n_H` of `r nrow(df)` patients
  (`r round(100 * n_H / nrow(df))`%), `r arm_means$treated_n` on ZDV + ddI and `r arm_means$control_n` on ddI. Their
  mean CD4 decline is `r f1(arm_means$treated_mean_decline)` under the combination against
  `r f1(arm_means$control_mean_decline)` under monotherapy.
- **Unadjusted.** Its oriented MD is `r f1(g$naive$est)` (`r f1(g$naive$lower)`, `r f1(g$naive$upper)`) — on its
  face the combination looks harmful here, the reverse of the trial's own direction, though the interval already
  covers 0.
- **The correction.** It removes a selection bias of `r sprintf("%.1f", g$selection_bias)` CD4 cells, over a family
  of `r g$n_family` candidates, leaving a two-term estimate of `r f1(g$debiased$est)`.
- **The field lower bound is `r f1(bounds$field_lower_H)`.** It does not reach 0, so **harm in this subgroup is not
  established**. What the data exclude is only a benefit larger than
  `r sprintf("%.0f", abs(bounds$field_lower_H))` CD4 cells; the bound clears
  `r cleared[["field lower, H-hat"]]` of the ladder.
- **Against the trial.** The whole-trial `r f1(ref[["whole trial"]])` lies inside what the bound allows, so these
  patients are not shown to differ from the trial as a whole. The unadjusted `r f1(g$naive$est)` is largely what
  the selection produced.

**The complement.**

- **Unadjusted and corrected.** `r n_Hc` patients: unadjusted `r f1(cc$naive$est)`, corrected
  `r f1(cc$debiased$est)`.
- **The field-s upper bound is `r f1(bounds$field_s_upper_Hc)`.** Outside the subgroup, **a benefit of at least
  `r sprintf("%.0f", abs(bounds$field_s_upper_Hc))` CD4 cells from the combination is established**; the bound
  clears `r cleared[["field-s upper, complement"]]`.
- **Against the trial.** The whole-trial `r f1(ref[["whole trial"]])` is within what it allows.

**The two-subgroup claim.**

- **The pair.** The Bonferroni pair is `r f1(bounds$bonf_lower_H)` for the selected subgroup and
  `r f1(bounds$bonf_upper_Hc)` for its complement, each at one-sided 0.975.
- **Why it is not conservative here.** Its simulated joint coverage is `r sprintf("%.3f", bounds$bonf_joint_prob)`,
  the calibrated split settles at γ = `r sprintf("%.3f", bounds$calib_gamma)`, Bonferroni's own α/2, and the aligned
  roots correlate at `r sprintf("%.2f", bounds$joint_corr)`.
- **What the claim amounts to.** Jointly, the complement keeps a benefit of at least
  `r sprintf("%.0f", abs(bounds$bonf_upper_Hc))` CD4 cells, while the selected subgroup is held only above
  `r f1(bounds$bonf_lower_H)`, which is no claim of harm. **So a claim that the two subgroups differ is not
  supported; the claim of benefit outside the subgroup is.**

**What this analysis does not establish.**

- **Coverage.** The bounds' coverage is established by simulation, including a mean-difference design built on
  these covariates. These data are that design's source, so this analysis is not an independent check of it.
- **The thresholds.** c1 = 10 and c2 = 5 CD4 cells are the applied document's choices, not a clinical calibration,
  and they sit far below the trial's own 27.6-cell benefit.
- **The rule.** `effMaxSG` at ε = 0.20 is this workstream's, not the applied document's `maxeffCons` (§1.1). The
  two rules select different subgroups on these data, both recorded in the stage-0 report's §6.
- **The candidate family.** MR's family is every size-eligible candidate, a superset of the one the search chose
  among, which the package notes inflates the selection-bias term.
- **The subset.** Only arms 1 and 3, as the applied document analyses them.
- **What was not run.** No full bootstrap, no operating-characteristics section, and no `compute_frontier_cis()`.
